Parco Nord — Milan, Italy

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 88 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

One of Milan's largest and most popular parks, heavily used by joggers, cyclists and families, with an active park-vigilance service patrolling daily. Coverage has documented occasional petty theft — phone snatching and car break-ins near the park edges — described as recurring but low-level. As with any large green space, it's sensible to stick to lit, populated paths after dark.

Frequently asked questions

Is Parco Nord safe?

Wandroz currently rates Parco Nord in Milan as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Milan during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Milan at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Milan publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Parco Nord safe at night?

At night, Parco Nord is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Milan. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Parco Nord a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Parco Nord's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Milan) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for Parco Nord?

Not an official government crime feed — Parco Nord's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used). An absence of recent negative coverage is treated as inconclusive, not as proof the area is safe. If you live in or know Parco Nord well, you can suggest a correction using the link below.
